newsitem.title: UK: Branson balloon to land in Algeria at first light.
newsitem.headline: Branson balloon to land in Algeria at first light.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Global Challenger balloon will land in Algeria when day breaks after his attempt to circle the world had to be abandoned because of technical problems, a spokesman for Branson said on Wednesday.

"They are going to try to land at first light if possible," project director Mike Kendrick told a hastily-arranged news conference at a London hotel. Earlier, officials had said the balloon would touch down in Algeria at about 0600 GMT.
"There are no injuries involved, this is purely technical," said Kendrick.
"The nature of the problem we are still trying to establish. I honestly can't tell you what it is, except that we know it's a ballast versus helium problem," he added.

Kendrick said the British tycoon's balloon had been as low as 4,000 feet (1,200 metres) earlier on Wednesday and was now at 12,000 feet (3,650 metres). It would pass over mountains and then attempt to land on flat terrain.

In an earlier statement, the Virgin Global Challenger control centre in London said the balloon would try to land in an area of Algeria about 50 to 70 miles (80 to 110 km) east of the border with Morocco.
